conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in their first arguments; λ>0 is the coefficient of the squared parameter norm, rather than its square root.
The same perturbation e enters yδ=Ax†+e and yh,δ=Ahx†+e, so dh=(A−Ah)x†=yδ−yh,δ.
The normal residual is rh,h=(Ah*Ah+λI)x̃h−Ah*yh,δ, whereas the solve vector is Rλ,hyh,δ−x̃h; consequently (Ah*Ah+λI)bsolve=−rh,h.
The definition supplies adjoints and assumes bijective shifted normal operators; the proposition assumes Countable Choice and obtains invertibility from its published Hilbert-space supplier.
The small-singular-value example uses changing spaces Rⁿ for integers n≥1, identical forward and discrete operators, and λn=n⁻⁴; it asserts no fixed infinite-dimensional discretization theorem.

load_bearing.statement: The five-channel error budget is the ordered tuple (bbias,bdata,boperator,bpre,bsolve), with bbias=x†−Rλy, bdata=Rλy−Rλyδ, boperator=(Rλ−Rλ,h)yh,δ, bpre=Rλdh, and bsolve=Rλ,hyh,δ−x̃h. The scalar total budget is the sum of the five channel norms.

Under Countable Choice and the stated compact Hilbert-space forward model, bounded finite-rank discrete map, λ>0, and noise bound, x†−x̃h=bbias+bdata+bpre+boperator+bsolve, and ‖x†−x̃h‖≤‖bbias‖+δ/(2√λ)+‖dh‖/(2√λ)+‖boperator‖+‖rh,h‖/λ. Operator-perturbation and evaluated-residual estimates require their separately stated certificates; no convergence rate is asserted.

published_dependencies.used_for: Compactness convention and the consequence that compact linear maps are bounded.
Real and complex Hilbert spaces with Cauchy-sequence completeness.
Exact choice assumption used by the proposition and Hilbert-space suppliers.
Adjoint identity with inner products linear in their first arguments.
Unit-ball operator norm, including zero spaces, and the conditional operator-channel bound.
Triangle inequality for real and complex induced norms.
Compactness of the explicit finite-dimensional operators in both assigned examples.
Bijectivity of shifted normal operators and inverse norm at most 1/λ under Countable Choice.
Data and pre-inversion amplification bounds of 1/(2√λ).
Concrete finite-matrix residual certificates, retaining arithmetic, coordinate, representation, and nonsingularity conditions.
Exact five-term refinement and explicit limits on implicit discretization and arithmetic guarantees.
Comparison with the additional minimum-norm and sequence-coupling hypotheses required for convergence.

seams_checked.note: The actual compact-model supplier permits arbitrary truths and imposes no injectivity or closed-range assumption. The error-budget definition preserves this interface and separately supplies adjoints and assumes shifted-normal bijectivity.

The page declares this prerequisite without directly citing either batch-4 item. Its solver contract and finite-status statements preserve the relevant distinction: algebraic residuals require stability certificates to bound errors, and continuous-to-discrete mesh accuracy is separately certified.

The experiment definition distinguishes additive observation errors from changes to the forward map. The companion forward-Euler example explicitly satisfies the budget interface and correctly computes dh=(A−Ah)1=1/2.
